_doc: B4 S1 (#381) — how big a bite of the calendar the player runs before they look again. ONE rule governs the ladder: you can skip ahead exactly as far as your people can cover for you. A day can only run headless when nothing escalates to the player, and what stops things escalating is a desk that is staffed and at threshold — so the door and the capability are the same fact and the player never learns a second rule. The doors live HERE (which coverage each bite requires); the predicates that decide whether a coverage fact holds live in code (`resolveBiteCoverage`, src/app/config.ts), reusing the same act-gate predicates the engine gates on. Naming the required coverage in the file is what keeps the two from drifting — the #371 news-progression-gating precedent, where a `hasDeskManager` boolean living in code was exactly what had to be deleted.
_coverageDoc: The facts a store can hold. `missingSentence` is stated VERBATIM by the picker when a bite's door is shut, and the sentences are written to stand alone so two of them read as one plain explanation when a bite needs both.

coverage.missingSentence: Your used car manager can't desk a discount on their own yet.
Nobody but you can approve a trade yet.
You haven't hired a general manager to run the store.

_bitesDoc: `days` is how many days the bite runs. The day is always open and is the LIVE floor — the runner is what a bite above the day uses. Rejected doors, recorded so they are not re-proposed: a bare tier number (opens the door while the desks are empty, so the bite would promise a week and halt on day 1), and an earned clean-day streak (a new persisted counter, and the player has to infer why the button came and went).
_stakesDoc: B4 S3 (#383) — what the player is WAGERING by picking this bite, stated at the picker before they commit. A bet you cannot read before placing is not a decision. The day carries none and is the only bite allowed to: it is the live floor, watched as it happens, so there is nothing to state in advance — and the schema refuses a bite above the day that omits it, so a fourth rung cannot ship blind. Stated verbatim by the picker; nothing is worded in the component.
_starBudgetDoc: B4 S2 (#382) — how many individual reactions the Reveal at THIS grain surfaces, wins/losses/crowns pooled. It rides the bite because the bite is the window the feed covers: seven days run through a day's budget throw away roughly seven times as much, and throw it away silently. It grows SUB-LINEARLY on purpose — seven days of reactions at seven times the stars is a scroll, not a beat — and what the budget cut is then stated as one line rather than dropped. The day's 5 is the shipped pre-#382 number, moved here from `tunables.reveal.drama.starBudget` (deleted) so there is one budget per grain and not two places to disagree.

bites.label: Run the Week
bites.stakes: Seven days run without you unless something needs you. The lot you stocked and the policy you set have to carry them.

bites.label: Run the Month
bites.stakes: Thirty days run without you unless something needs you. The lot you stocked, the policy you set and the people you hired have to carry them.

_haltsDoc: A bite stops at the first moment the store needs a human, and the bite is OVER — the player picks again from wherever the clock now sits. There is no queued remainder and no auto-resume: a run that silently continued past the thing that interrupted it would be the bite making the player's decision for them. Each sentence is stated verbatim by the Reveal. `owner_interrupt` (B4 S4, #384) is the one halt that names WHO stopped the run: its `{subject}` slot is filled from the raised moment's own copy in `data/owner-interrupts.json`, so the halt cadence is written once here and the subject once there.

halts.sentence: A deal came to your desk, so the run stopped there.
The store ran out of money, so the run stopped there.
The month was graded, so the run stopped there.
